traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 213 Meliaceae: trees or shrubs, mostly with hard scented wood (mahogany, cedrela), very rarely nearly herbaceous; leaves alternate, mostly pinnate; no stipules; flowers regular, mostly bisexual; stamens mostly 8 or 10, their filaments mostly joined in a tube; ovary superior, often of 3 to 5 cells; fruit a berry or capsule, rarely a drupe, the seeds sometimes winged (mahogany).

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia, Meliaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers apparently cryptically unisexual. Weighting toward dioecious inferred (Aglaia, Dysoxylum); low confidence.
